title: Sell Mineral Rights in Jerusalem, AR
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Jerusalem, AR
metaDescription: Jerusalem, AR (Conway County) mineral rights in the Fayetteville Shale gas trend. Small legacy interests from the 2000s drilling boom near Morrilton.
heroLead: Jerusalem is a small Conway County community that saw its share of Fayetteville Shale leasing during the field's peak years, even if it never made headlines the way the counties to the east did.
intro: Conway County sits toward the western edge of the Fayetteville Shale's productive core, and operators leased broadly across the county during the boom even where drilling turned out to be less dense than in Faulkner or White counties. Mineral owners around Jerusalem often hold interests that were leased once, may or may not have seen a well, and haven't generated much attention since gas prices dropped after 2012.

sections.heading: Western Edge of the Play
paragraphs: Because Jerusalem sits closer to the western margin of the Fayetteville Shale's core productive area, well density here has historically been lower than in counties further east. That doesn't mean mineral rights here have no value; it means valuation depends more heavily on specific unit and lease status than on a general assumption about the county.

sections.heading: Sorting Out an Inherited Interest
paragraphs: As with most rural Conway County land, mineral interests around Jerusalem frequently passed through inheritance without formal probate. The Conway County Circuit Clerk's office in Morrilton holds the deed and probate records needed to establish clean ownership, and an affidavit of heirship is often sufficient to resolve gaps in the chain of title.

faqs.question: Is there active gas production right around Jerusalem?
faqs.answer: It varies by tract. Conway County saw broad leasing during the Fayetteville Shale boom but somewhat less drilling density than counties further east, so some tracts near Jerusalem have producing wells nearby and others don't.

faqs.question: My family's old lease from the boom years never mentioned a specific well. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes, leases were often signed broadly across an area before operators finalized drilling plans, so many landowners leased without ever having a well placed on their specific tract.

faqs.question: What if I don't know exactly which relative originally leased the mineral rights?
faqs.answer: The Conway County Circuit Clerk's deed index can usually be searched by name to identify the original lease and trace ownership forward to you.

faqs.question: Is it worth getting an interest near Jerusalem evaluated even if I'm not sure it's producing?
faqs.answer: Yes. A quick records check costs you nothing and tells you whether the interest is leased, producing, or open, which is the information needed before deciding whether selling makes sense.

faqs.question: How does a buyer treat a Conway County interest that was leased but has no recorded well nearby?
faqs.answer: It's evaluated on position and comparable activity in the surrounding area rather than an existing royalty history, since none exists yet for that specific tract.
